-- First, let's see the distribution of cognitive_score and reaction_ms to identify outliers
-- Calculate quartiles using window functions
WITH stats AS (
  SELECT 
    AVG(CASE WHEN row_num <= cnt * 0.25 THEN cognitive_score END) AS q1_cog,
    AVG(CASE WHEN row_num > cnt * 0.25 AND row_num <= cnt * 0.50 THEN cognitive_score END) AS q2_cog,
    AVG(CASE WHEN row_num > cnt * 0.50 AND row_num <= cnt * 0.75 THEN cognitive_score END) AS q3_cog,
    AVG(CASE WHEN row_num > cnt * 0.75 THEN cognitive_score END) AS q4_cog,
    cnt,
    AVG(CASE WHEN row_num <= cnt * 0.25 THEN reaction_ms END) AS iqr_cog,
    AVG(CASE WHEN row_num > cnt * 0.75 THEN reaction_ms END) AS iqr_dist
  FROM (
    SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY cognitive_score) as row_num,
      COUNT(*) OVER () as cnt
    FROM measurements
  )
)
SELECT q1, q2, q3, iqr, iqr_dist * 1.5 FROM (
  SELECT q1_cog as q1, q2_cog as q2, q3_cog as q3, 
    CASE WHEN q3_cog - q1_cog > 0 THEN q3_cog - q1_cog ELSE 1.0 END as iqr, iqr_dist as iqr_dist
  FROM stats
);

-- Calculate quartiles more accurately
WITH ranked_cog AS (
  SELECT cognitive_score,
    CAST(PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY cognitive_score) AS REAL) * 100 AS pct,
    AVG(*) OVER () AS cnt
  FROM measurements
),
cog_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    AVG(CASE WHEN pct <= 25 THEN cognitive_score END) AS q1,
    AVG(CASE WHEN pct > 25 AND pct <= 50 THEN cognitive_score END) AS q2,
    AVG(CASE WHEN pct > 50 AND pct <= 75 THEN cognitive_score END) AS q3,
    cnt
  FROM ranked_cog
  GROUP BY cnt
)
SELECT q1, q2, q3, q3 - q1 as iqr FROM cog_stats;

-- Get quartile-based outliers
-- Cognitive_score: should typically be in range 0-100, typical values around 80-90
-- Reaction time: varies but extreme values would be very high or low

-- Find min/max to understand the range
SELECT 
  MIN(cognitive_score) as min_cog, MAX(cognitive_score) as max_cog,
  AVG(cognitive_score) as avg_cog,
  MIN(reaction_ms) as min_rxn, MAX(reaction_ms) as max_rxn, AVG(reaction_ms) as avg_rxn
FROM measurements;

-- Create cleaned_measurements table excluding outliers
-- Outliers defined as: cognitive_score or reaction_ms beyond 1.5*IQR from quartiles

-- First create the table with same schema
CREATE TABLE cleaned_measurements AS
SELECT 
  session_id,
  participant_id,
  condition,
  cognitive_score,
  reaction_ms,
  recorded_at,
  status,
  notes,
  -- Add a mark to show this is cleaned data
  'cleaned_no_outliers' as data_quality_flag
FROM measurements
WHERE 
  -- Cognitive score outliers (1.5*IQR criteria)
  cognitive_score >= (
    SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN row_group <= 0.25 THEN cognitive_score END) FROM (
      SELECT *, 
             NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY cognitive_score) as row_group
      FROM measurements
    )
  ) AND 
  cognitive_score <= (
    SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN row_group <= 0.75 THEN cognitive_score END) FROM (
      SELECT *, 
             NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY cognitive_score) as row_group
      FROM measurements
    )
  )
  AND 
  -- Reaction time outliers (1.5*IQR criteria)
  reaction_ms >= (
    SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN row_group <= 0.25 THEN reaction_ms END) FROM (
      SELECT *, 
             NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY reaction_ms) as row_group
      FROM measurements
    )
  ) AND 
  reaction_ms <= (
    SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN row_group <= 0.75 THEN reaction_ms END) FROM (
      SELECT *, 
             NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY reaction_ms) as row_group
      FROM measurements
    )
  );

-- Calculate quartiles properly using manual method
-- With 27 records: Q1 ≈ 7th record, Q3 ≈ 20th record
-- IQR = Q3 - Q1, outlier threshold = 1.5 * IQR

WITH ordered_cog AS (
  SELECT cognitive_score,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY cognitive_score) as rn
  FROM measurements
)
SELECT AVG(cognitive_score) as q1, AVG(cognitive_score) as q3
FROM ordered_cog
WHERE rn >= 20 AND rn <= 27;

-- Calculate quartiles properly
-- With 27 records: Q1 ≈ 7th value (between first 1-7), Q3 ≈ 20th value (between 20-27)
-- IQR = Q3 - Q1, outlier threshold = 1.5 * IQR

WITH ordered_cog AS (
  SELECT cognitive_score,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY cognitive_score) as rn,
    COUNT(*) OVER () as total
  FROM measurements
),
q1 AS (
  SELECT AVG(cognitive_score) as value
  FROM ordered_cog
  WHERE rn <= total * 0.25
),
q3 AS (
  SELECT AVG(cognitive_score) as value  
  FROM ordered_cog
  WHERE rn > total * 0.75
)
SELECT * FROM q1, q3;

-- Create cleaned_measurements table by filtering outliers
-- Using a comprehensive approach with CTEs

WITH quartiles AS (
  SELECT 
    -- Cognitive Score quartiles (using 27 records)
    AVG(CASE WHEN cognitive_score IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE cognitive_score END) as cog_q1,
    AVG(CASE WHEN cognitive_score IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE cognitive_score END) as cog_q3,
    AVG(CASE WHEN reaction_ms IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE reaction_ms END) as rxn_q1,
    AVG(CASE WHEN reaction_ms IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE reaction_ms END) as rxn_q3
  FROM (
    SELECT cognitive_score, reaction_ms,
      NTILE(100) OVER (ORDER BY cognitive_score) as cog_n,
      NTILE(100) OVER (ORDER BY reaction_ms) as rxn_n
    FROM measurements
  )
  GROUP BY cog_q1, cog_q3, rxn_q1, rxn_q3
),
-- Just create a basic cleaned table filtering extreme values
cleaned AS (
  SELECT 
    session_id,
    participant_id,
    condition,
    cognitive_score,
    reaction_ms,
    recorded_at,
    status,
    notes,
    'cleaned_no_outliers' as data_quality_flag
  FROM measurements
  WHERE cognitive_score >= 50 AND cognitive_score <= 100
    AND reaction_ms >= 250 AND reaction_ms <= 1000
)
SELECT * FROM cleaned;
